semantic_review_facts.scope: All19/21 historical mutating npm callers and their direct changing input owners
facts: Every full current npm invocation statement is byte-equal to its authenticated immutable historical parent, including same npmToolingOptions(argv), cwd, env, timeout and encoding. v1 records each exact statement and source identity.

The shared owner and fixed root/package/config inputs retain original bytes. Its fresh process cache, blank config files, inherited npm/auth removal, fixed public registry, workspaces/global false, ignore_scripts true and online-revalidation options therefore retain their historical source behavior.
All six immutable brace-specific source inputs remain physically identical. This review does not modify or reinterpret their original validation receipts.

Meaning-changing browser dependency generation was individually reviewed, not treated as hash-only drift: fixed plan supplies exact names/versions; packed artifact may select validated supported line/advertised ranges and supply own local package bytes. No artifact dependency fields or selectors supply npm argv, registry, workspace or helper flags.

New packed/browser/ripple/Sass fixture source and assertion imports are emitted/used after npm installation; they do not supply the generated package.json install arguments. Exact source images and supporting data remain required bindings.

semantic_review_facts.scope: Exact recursive tests code population1231/main and1373/21 from census v2; Python AST launches plus JavaScript process primitives/imported names inspected as source
facts: Python subprocess calls select literal Node/Git/Python commands or sys.executable/pinned NODE variables. The one parameter-only RulesJsBuildAdmissionTests.probe wrapper has exactly three fixed source calls: two Node probes and one sys.executable ledger-patch script. No test Python subprocess selects a package/advisory/config value as executable/npm argv.

JavaScript executable heads are literal commands or process.execPath, except three current tests selecting trusted CHROME_BIN/existing Chromium paths: template_control_flow_probe.mjs, table_no_data_cell_probe.mjs and table_column_class_probe.mjs. Browser CLI argument arrays are authored source; no selector or package-manifest value selects npm arguments.

Node worker target paths in these tests are fixed current probes or own generated temporary workers from authenticated/owned subject code. Tests retain the existing dependency/runtime execution boundary; this is not dependency code review or qualification.

Npm-looking source in npm_tooling_caller_probe, viewport_tooling_requalification_probe and test_tool_advisory_dispositions is AST/source-comparison or refusal mutation DATA. The synthetic added-query sources are written into fixture roots and passed to physical source validation, not executed.

test_rc_run_writer_and_sealer creates own temporary npm/pnpm shell stubs printing synthetic-version only for coordinator version observations. test_toolchain patches subprocess.run with an in-process fake for npm version. Neither is a real new mutating npm route.
The actual optional npm CLI test route is described independently below; it must not disappear behind the19/21 literal mutating caller count.

NGX_NPM_PROFILE_CLI is inherited trusted-operator environment selecting an explicit Node CLI path. Exact argv are --version and config list --json. Version must equal11.19.0; isolated helper options use fresh temp cache/config and assert resulting registry/workspaces/ignore_scripts/cache flags.

This route existed in the historical isolation checkpoint evidence and its current bytes match the separately recorded architecture input hash. It performs configuration observation rather than install/query/sbom/exec/run-script/pack/publish. No package/advisory/manifest field reaches CLI path or command text.

A current profile must explicitly say19/21 are mutating tool-owned invocation records, with this exact optional read-only route separate. It cannot describe every process in the source graph as one of the19/21 calls.

The floor parent uses fixed sh -c command -v npm, realpaths the resulting CLI, requires suffix/npm-cli.js and exact pinned toolchain npm --version. It passes that CLI path in NGX_FLOOR_NPM_CLI to the fixed packed consumer runner.

When a floor case is selected, the consumer replaces executable npm with process.execPath and prepends that absolute CLI path. It forwards the same historical helper-guarded install argv/options; it does not accept another npm subcommand or registry/selector flag.

This indirection is unchanged source from the historical profile. Trusted operator PATH/direct-floor CLI overrides remain outside any claim that arbitrary host binaries are authenticated by source hashing.

These byte-unchanged historical CLI sources intentionally accept inherited MIGRATE_LEGACY_BEFORE_WRITE and use spawnSync(hook,{shell:true}) only during --apply with no blocking migration diagnostics. It is an arbitrary trusted-operator shell seam and could name npm; it is not a maintained npmToolingOptions-owned invocation.

The maintained transaction driver clears inherited hook and NODE_OPTIONS before every child, then supplies only two own generated Node hooks: append a concurrent-edit marker to an owned temp file or process.exit(3). No artifact/package/advisory/evidence field supplies those hook commands.

Other CLI consumers preserve historical trusted-operator environment behavior; the profile must not expand into a claim about arbitrary operator hook commands. This is source/call scope accounting, not a new vulnerability verdict, remediation or acceptance of residual risk.

semantic_review_facts.scope: New acquisition/source-evidence/history Python+JS and existing generic process wrappers
facts: Source acquisition families launch fixed git command arrays and fetch/read immutable upstream blobs as DATA; selection is bounded by exact SHA/path sets and validation. They do not invoke npm or write a generated npm consumer manifest/registry/cache setting. No acquisition was run here.

New source readers launch fixed git, rg, tar or Node/Python source-review workers; their module targets are fixed source or finite authenticated catalogues. Historical runners execute selected authenticated snapshots when separately invoked; this review recovered old blobs as DATA only and ran none.

Finite dynamic first-party module constructions were inspected: fixture lifecycle uses seven hardcoded families; chip audit and chip focus native loops use fixed local module tuples; slider range requires one of nine module names plus pinned prior rows. These expand to current scripts images in the exact primary census.

Computed external compiler/runtime imports retain the existing trusted developer/compiler or authenticated peer-subject boundary. They do not accept npm commands/argv from package/advisory fields. Arbitrary exported test overrides/root/loader callbacks are not asserted safe by this static profile.

Existing shelljs archive creator interpolates operator suffix/package output paths into tar commands; inherited code and not an npm invocation. Existing Node/Chromium/compiler process wrappers retain authored argv and source-owned targets; no new meaningful route to an unsupported npm command was identified.

semantic_review_facts.scope: Resolved outside-primary executable support under compatibility/rc, product/reference/testing roots and handoff tools
facts: Actual process primitives outside scripts/tests are fixed Git source reads, Node current/generated subject probes and Python fixed Node probes. The expectation-model exec matches and Angular NgZone.run matches are RegExp/protocol methods, not process launches. Exact source rows remain bound; no compatibility/Sass filename exclusion is used.

Historical preimage .mjs/.py sources found through literal code-path scanning remain source-comparison DATA unless an actual reviewed current execution edge selects them. Presence in the broad physical support table does not confer permission to execute historical/advisory validation programs or redefine their verdicts.

Committed standalone CLI support files are generated-distribution source already in Git; their transaction hook is explicitly scoped above. Uncommitted dist outputs remain unadmitted as current first-party source.

core-alias-identity-smoke directly imports the already-built legacy-core FESM only to assert exported token/helper identities and values and print a report. It does not import a process launcher or use artifact values to construct npm arguments/manifest/config.

compare-core-declarations parses already-built declarations as TypeScript DATA and launches fixed alias identity checker. Its untracked declaration paths are build artifacts, not committed source admissions.

Both producer sources are unchanged primary images from the old profile. The unresolved generated file identity is retained as unadmitted and belongs to separate built/packed artifact qualification. This source-only npm profile cannot qualify those artifact bytes or claim their runtime behavior. No fallback reader or filename waiver is authorized.

conditional_scope_conclusion.supported: The exact maintained tool-owned npm install/ci/local-pack invocations and separately recorded read-only version/config routes preserve their historical command, isolation and source-owned input preconditions at both committed cuts, provided the new checker enforces the complete exact current primary/support/discovery bindings and leaves historical archive/selector/brace evidence unchanged.
not_supported: A global claim that arbitrary operator PATH/NODE_OPTIONS/compiler roots/test loader overrides/MIGRATE_LEGACY_BEFORE_WRITE cannot select code or invoke npm.
Admission of untracked generated dist, third-party dependencies, historical snapshot execution, advisory validation artifacts or arbitrary new callers.
